notes: Read every target unit and preceding context. Resolve the opening continuation to Cold War targeting assumptions; anchor the unnamed administration to 2000. Preserve tactical versus strategic weapons, the Russia analogy, as-many-as-possible limits, safety mechanisms, and Republican-presidency conditional commitments.

claims.claim_text: Opposition to letting Cold War targeting assumptions dictate the size of the U.S. nuclear arsenal.
The U.S. administration in office in 2000 appears not to recognize the obsolescence of letting Cold War targeting assumptions determine U.S. nuclear arsenal size.
Support for U.S. cooperation with other nuclear-armed countries to remove as many weapons as possible from high-alert status and reduce accidental or unauthorized launch risks.
Keeping nuclear weapons on high-alert status is an unnecessary remnant of Cold War confrontation.
In 1991, the United States invited the Soviet Union to join it in removing tactical nuclear weapons from their arsenals.
Large tactical nuclear weapons reductions were achieved within months of the 1991 U.S.-Soviet initiative.
The 1991 U.S.-Soviet tactical nuclear weapons reductions quickly made the world much safer.
Commitment under a Republican U.S. president to invite Russia to make strategic nuclear weapons reductions modeled on the 1991 U.S.-Soviet tactical nuclear initiative.
Support for U.S. readiness to lead by example in strategic nuclear weapons reductions, in the interests of both the United States and the world.
Proposed U.S.-Russian strategic nuclear weapons reductions could improve global nuclear security and safety.
Republican leadership offers opportunities for the United States both to defend against nuclear threats and to reduce nuclear arsenals and tensions.
The United States can build strong missile defenses, sharply reduce its nuclear weapons and reduce confrontation with Russia.
Commitment under a Republican U.S. president to build strong missile defenses, sharply reduce U.S. nuclear weapons and reduce confrontation with Russia.
